title: Tell Your Story
description: Integrate the Unit language to complete a sustained B1 mission about experiences & storytelling.

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to integrate the Unit language to complete a sustained B1 mission about experiences & storytelling. The central language focus is integrated experience and narrative review. In the context of experiences & storytelling, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At B1, connected communication matters more than isolated accuracy. Give the main information, link events or reasons, and respond to a follow-up without relying on memorized one-line answers.

blocks.english: This example illustrates in the end clearly.
blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.

blocks.english: We should consider look back on carefully.
blocks.explanation: This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “This example illustrates in the end clearly.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “We should consider look back on carefully.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: integrated experience and narrative review. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by integrated experience and narrative review; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For tell your story, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction. This sixth Lesson consolidates Lessons 1–5 and introduces no major new grammar. Select among the Unit patterns according to the communicative need.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.

segments.text: To begin with, This example illustrates in the end clearly. We should consider look back on carefully.
In this situation, We should consider look back on carefully. It turned out that.
From another perspective, It turned out that. What happened next?
More specifically, What happened next? The experience taught me that.
Even so, The experience taught me that. Our response should account for memorable experience.
